newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat defence chief to US for talks, surgery - paper.
newsitem.headline: Croat defence chief to US for talks, surgery - paper.

text.p: Croatian Defence Minister Gojko Susak will fly to the United States on Tuesday for talks on the peace process in Bosnia and the return of the last Serb-held area of Croatia to Zagreb's control, state media said.

But the independent weekly Nacional, quoting a doctor from one of Zagreb's main hospitals, said an important reason for Susak's trip was medical -- another operation to combat cancer which appeared to have spread from a lung.

Susak is due to meet U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry and other U.S. government leaders to discuss the U.N.-supervised reintegration of Serb-held eastern Slavonia into Croatia and the implementation of the Dayton peace accords on Bosnia.
State radio said Susak and U.S. officials would also discuss Croatia's aspirations to membership in NATO's Partnership for Peace programme.
Susak, 50, regarded as President Franjo Tudjman's right-hand man, is also expected to sign a deal to buy U.S. helicopters for the Croatian army.
The Croatian government disclosed in March that Susak underwent surgery at Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington D.C. but did not reveal the nature of his illness.
Nacional said the second round of surgery might take place in the same hospital.

Susak, defence minister since Croatia's declaration of independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, masterminded a buildup of the government army which retook territory held by pro-Yugoslav rebel Serbs in blitz offensives last summer.
He is the leader of the omni-powerful nationalist lobby of the Bosnian Croats from Herzegovina in the Zagreb government.
Susak lived 20 years in Canada as a businessman before returning with other prominent, affluent Croat emigres to help Tudjman guide Croatia to statehood.
